title: Resolve runtime java via Gradle tool chain provider

timeline.body:
Using gradle toolchain support in gradle requires refactoring how the composite build is composed. 
We added three toolchain resolver
1. Resolver for resolving defined bundled version from oracle as openjdk
2. Resolve all available jdks from Adoption
3. Resolve archived Oracle jdk distributions. 

We should be able to remove the JdkDownloadPlugin altogether without having that in place, but we'll do that in a separate PR.

Fixes #95094

We have some tests left that fail due to gradle toolchain support lacking well configuration cache behavior. see https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/fx2ra3p5l4rfc/tests/:build-tools-internal:integTest/org.elasticsearch.gradle.internal.test.rest.RestResourcesPluginFuncTest/restResources%20does%20nothing%20when%20there%20are%20no%20tests?focused-exception-line=0-23&top-execution=1
The existing logic doesn't work with the reworked composition setup

+import org.gradle.api.provider.Property

+import org.gradle.platform.Architecture
+import org.gradle.platform.BuildPlatform
+import org.gradle.platform.OperatingSystem
+import spock.lang.Specification
+
+import static org.gradle.platform.Architecture.X86_64
+import static org.gradle.platform.OperatingSystem.MAC_OS
+
+abstract class AbstractToolchainResolverSpec extends Specification {
+
+    def "resolves #os #arch #vendor jdk #langVersion"() {
+        given:
+        def resolver = resolverImplementation()
+
+        when:
+        Optional<JavaToolchainDownload> download = resolver.resolve(request(JavaLanguageVersion.of(langVersion), vendor, platform(os, arch)))
+
+        then:
+        download.get().uri == URI.create(expectedUrl)
+        where:
+
+        [langVersion, vendor, os, arch, expectedUrl] << supportedRequests()
+    }
+
+
+    def "does not resolve #os #arch #vendor jdk #langVersion"() {
+        given:
+        def resolver = resolverImplementation()
+
+        when:
+        Optional<JavaToolchainDownload> download = resolver.resolve(request(JavaLanguageVersion.of(langVersion), vendor, platform(os, arch)))
+
+        then:
+        download.isEmpty()
+        where:
+        [langVersion, vendor, os, arch] << unsupportedRequests()
+    }
+
+    abstract JavaToolchainResolver resolverImplementation();
+
+    abstract supportedRequests();
+
+    abstract unsupportedRequests();
+
+    JavaToolchainRequest request(JavaLanguageVersion languageVersion = null,
+                                 JvmVendorSpec vendorSpec = anyVendor(),
+                                 BuildPlatform platform = platform()) {
+        JavaToolchainSpec toolchainSpec = Mock()
+        Property<JavaLanguageVersion> languageVersionProperty = Mock()
+        _ * toolchainSpec.getLanguageVersion() >> languageVersionProperty
+        _ * languageVersionProperty.get() >> languageVersion
+
+        Property<JvmVendorSpec> vendorSpecProperty = Mock()
+        _ * vendorSpecProperty.get() >> vendorSpec
+        _ * toolchainSpec.getVendor() >> vendorSpecProperty
+
+        JavaToolchainRequest request = Mock()
+
+        _ * request.getJavaToolchainSpec() >> toolchainSpec
+        _ * request.getBuildPlatform() >> platform
+        return request
+    }
+
+    JvmVendorSpec anyVendor() {
+        return new AnyJvmVendorSpec();
+    }
+
+    BuildPlatform platform(OperatingSystem os = MAC_OS, Architecture arch = X86_64) {
+        return new TestBuildPlatform(operatingSystem: os, architecture: arch)
+    }
+
+
+    static class TestBuildPlatform implements BuildPlatform {
+        OperatingSystem operatingSystem
+        Architecture architecture
+    }
+
+    static class AnyJvmVendorSpec extends JvmVendorSpec {
+        @Override
+        boolean matches(String vendor) {
+            return vendor == "any"
+        }
+
+        @Override
+        String toString() {
+            return "any"
+        }
+    }
+}

timeline.body:
I'm wondering if we want to do this. I'd feel better if our testing was using the _actual_ bundled JDK. That is, the exact vendor/minor version we bundle vs an "equivalent".

Until we completely remove the need for our own jdk download plugin I'd suggest we revert this bit and use the resolved bundled jdk for testing until we can resolve our bundled JDK via the Gradle toolchain support.

reply.body:
But we would resolve the exact same version as it would resolve the bundled jdk first. The order of
the resolver decorations in settings.gradle matter.
We can also change it to explicitly request oracle as a vendor. This guarantees we always resolve the exact bundled jdk even in the small chance scenario of temporal network issue with resolving the openjdk from oracle moving on to use adoption instead.

Ok, that makes sense. Yeah, I had thought about introducing some kind of custom vendor (i.e. "bundled") that's only resolved by our bundled JDK resolver so there's no risk of using something different. I think if we can give the bundled resolver priority and control that then it's fine.

timeline.body: Didn't we resolve the configuration cache issue here in a separate PR?

reply.body: Not really. Just matching to ordering of the parameter.  🤓

timeline.body: Do we want to keep the `JAVAX_HOME` environment variables at all? I'm leaning towards removing it entirely if we are auto-resolving things. That way at least it's consistent and we can remove the logic and documentation for this.

reply.body: We could, but I would not want to do that in this PR. I wonder if there would be a downside in CI environments as the java runtimes are part of the image. We would probably need to change our gradle cache filling to also resolve required toolchains we test against.
We don't use this feature in CI at all. In CI we explicitly set `RUNTIME_JAVA_HOME` to the specific JDK we are intending to test.

timeline.body: Should we use a thread-safe data structure here? Is toolchain resolution done in parallel at all?

reply.body: It is not. But maybe with configuration cache it will be at one point. I changed it to ConcurentHashMap just to be safe

timeline.body: In what cases do we specifically request an Oracle vendor JDK where the equivalent adoptium one won't work?

reply.body: I thought this would be neat if we want to test against oracle jdks specifically in certain situations.

timeline.body: Keep in mind that when the bundled JDK is an initial release, the version string is something like `20+3` and then subsequent patches are `20.0.1+6` or similar. I don't think this will work in the former case as it would report `20+3` as the major version.
